input.title: Santa Monica algorithmic rental pricing software ban
input.key_value: ban on sale and use of algorithmic devices using competitor data
input.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, algorithmic software that uses competitor data to advise on rent prices or whether to leave units vacant. Tenants can raise violations as an affirmative defense in eviction cases, and tenants or the city can sue; penalties are $1,000 per offense or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees.
input.quoted_span: The Santa Monica ordinance defines prohibited "algorithmic devices" as software that uses competitor data to advise landlords on rent pricing or whether to leave units vacant

input.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment: eviction only for just cause
input.key_value: Eviction only for enumerated just causes; cause stated in notice; copy filed with Rent Control Board within 3 days
input.requirement: Landlords of controlled units may not demand possession, serve a notice to quit, or sue to evict unless a listed just cause applies (e.g. nonpayment, uncured material breach or nuisance, owner/relative move-in, demolition, Ellis withdrawal). The notice must state the cause and a copy must be filed with the Rent Control Board within 3 days (except 3-day pay-or-quit notices). Retaliatory evictions are barred, and owner move-in requires good-faith occupancy within 60 days for at least two years, with protections for tenants 62+ or disabled with 5+ years or terminally ill.
input.coverage_conditions: Controlled rental units as defined in §1801(c).
input.exemptions: Same exemptions as controlled rental units; single family homes not rented July 1, 1984 (§1815); State Park/tidelands property (§1820).
input.quoted_span:

for possession of a rental unit, threatening to terminate a tenancy, serving any notice to quit or
other eviction notice

input.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment: maximum allowable rents and annual general adjustment
input.key_value: 75% of CPI, min 0%, max 3% annual general adjustment
input.requirement: Rents on controlled units cannot exceed the Rent Control Board's maximum allowable rent (MAR). Each September 1 the MAR rises by 75% of the regional CPI change, but never less than 0% or more than 3% (3.0% in 2024). Landlords may not raise rent if they have not complied with the Article (e.g. registration fees) or have uncorrected housing-code violations. Owners may pass half the registration fee through to tenants, plus limited property-tax surcharges for pre-March 2018 tenancies (capped at $35 or 4% of MAR).
input.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in Santa Monica except exempt units (hotels, institutions, owner-occupied up to 3 units, units constructed after adoption of the Article, certain single family homes per §1815, State Park/tidelands property per §1820).
input.exemptions: Transient hotel/motel units; hospitals, convents, dormitories; certain government units; owner-occupied dwellings of 3 or fewer units; units constructed after adoption of the Article (not conversions); non-profit child care/social service units; single family homes not rented July 1, 1984; State Park/tidelands property. Exemptions are granted by the Board on owner application.
input.quoted_span:
in no event shall the general
adjustment be less than zero percent or greater than three (3) percent
